notes: GATE P1 REGRESSION RERUN. Same harness and same shape as 2026-08-13-macos-cache-backed-tar-e2e, rebuilt from scratch so that every release carries the new authenticated delta-v1 release identity in its minisign trusted comment. The point of the rerun is not the ratio -- it reproduces the earlier one -- but that adding an authenticated identity check to all three install paths did not close the delta path. WHY THIS PROVES THE AUTHENTICATED PATH RAN, rather than legacy compatibility: a signature with no delta-v1 binding parses as Legacy, and a Legacy binding makes both delta paths UNAVAILABLE by construction in plan_update, so a full download is the only reachable outcome. Transition 2 installed from a tar delta. It could not have done so under a legacy signature, so the identity was parsed, was authenticated, and matched on app id, version, platform, digest, size and representation. One decoded comment, from manifest-1.0.1.json: 'delta-v1 app:dev.chahdane.delta-updater-example v:1.0.1 plat:darwin-aarch64 rep:app-tar-gz-v1 b3:82f2a22d2b70240b9e3bd206a42f1c4a063262b3cafb4d119b2886258b2e3a71 sz:4171052 ts:1786656490'. The three main binaries hash to a99873d5..., 1c983ea9... and e60c3f22... (SHA-256) and are asserted pairwise distinct, so the versions are genuinely different builds and not relabelled copies. Transition 1 is a full download because the cache starts empty, which is the honest cold-start behaviour and not a fallback. The degradation case corrupts the cached base blob and confirms the update still completes, via a full download rather than a tar delta. CONFOUNDER, unchanged from the earlier run and stated again so the ratio is not over-read: the only source difference between versions is a version string, so 15.4% is a best case for this shape of change and not a general expectation. Tree dirty because the e2e harness --app-id threading was still uncommitted at run time; it was committed immediately after, unmodified.
artifact_provenance: examples/desktop-app/e2e/build-three-versions.sh /private/tmp/delta-p1-e2e, which runs `cargo tauri build --features e2e-control` three times against examples/desktop-app with only the version string changed, then publishes both releases with the delta-release binary built from this tree, passing --app-id derived from tauri.conf.json's identifier and --require-tar-layer. delta-release derives the signed digest and size from the final artifact it just wrote, so the identity cannot describe an artifact other than the one published. Replayed by examples/desktop-app/e2e/run-tar-e2e.sh against a local HTTP server; the app under test is the real bundled .app, launched and relaunched between transitions so that promotion is licensed by what actually ran.
